questions.question: You’re at a café and your friend’s coffee is spilled on their shirt. What would be the most appropriate way to apologise?
options: I’m so sorry about this! I’ll get you a new shirt.
This is your fault—you didn’t look where you were going.
Oh, it’s fine! Don’t worry about it.
I didn’t mean to do that, but I’ll pay for the damage.
questions.answer: I’m so sorry about this! I’ll get you a new shirt.

questions.question: Your colleague suggests, ‘Let’s try this new marketing strategy—it might work better.’ How would you respond if you were unsure but open to feedback?
options: That’s a great idea! I’ll definitely try it.
I think we should stick with the old one—it’s been working well.
I’m not sure, but I’d be happy to give it a go if you think it’ll help.
No, that’s not a good plan at all. It’s too risky.
questions.answer: I’m not sure, but I’d be happy to give it a go if you think it’ll help.

questions.question: At a family gathering, your aunt says, ‘I really enjoyed your new book—it’s fantastic!’ How would you politely respond to express your agreement and add a personal touch?
options: Thanks! I’m glad you liked it. It was a lot of work, though.
Oh, you’re so sweet—I didn’t even think it was good enough.
That’s really kind of you to say. I’m glad you enjoyed it too!
I don’t know why you’d like it—I wrote it badly.
questions.answer: That’s really kind of you to say. I’m glad you enjoyed it too!

questions.question: A friend asks, ‘Do you think we should move to that new apartment? It’s much bigger than ours.’ What would be the most appropriate way to politely disagree while offering an alternative?
options: Yes, absolutely! It’s perfect—let’s go now.
I don’t think it’s a good idea. Our current place is comfortable enough.
That sounds great, but I think we should wait until next year—we’ll need more furniture first.
No, we should sell our house instead—it’s too expensive to move.
questions.answer: I don’t think it’s a good idea. Our current place is comfortable enough.

questions.question: Your boss asks, ‘Can you help me with this presentation next week?’ What would be the most appropriate way to politely decline while offering to assist later?
options: No, I can’t—I have too much work to do right now.
I’d love to help, but I’m not available until after the weekend.
That’s not my job—I’m not qualified for that.
You’re too busy—find someone else to do it.
questions.answer: I’d love to help, but I’m not available until after the weekend.
